newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Japan APEC plan falls short on farm products.
newsitem.headline: Japan APEC plan falls short on farm products.

text.p: Japan unveiled on Friday a set of market-opening measures at the ministerial meeting of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum but fell short on farm imports.

Japan's Individual Action Plan, a 92-page outline of what it would do to spur liberalisation of trade and investment in the 18-member APEC, was submitted to the ministerial meeting by Trade Minister Shinji Sato.
But the plan did not include measures to open up rice and other politically-sensitive farm products beyond those promised at the Uruguay Round of multilateral trade negotiations.
Critics in Japan had said Tokyo should liberalise trade where it hurt most in order to be respected as a leader in the APEC forum.

Japan's promised deregulatory measures include moves to align Japanese industrial, agricultural and electrical appliance standards to international ones, such as the International Organisation of Standardisation (ISO).
Japan will also increase the number of foreign testing institutions for foodstuffs and streamline inspection of food imports.
Visas for businessmen from fellow APEC members will be extended to five years from the current three, and Japan will accept all tourist groups from APEC members.

In telecommunications, Japan will lift stringent controls on telephone networks, improve access to electronic commerce methods and open a satellite compound in Kobe, western Japan, for APEC's integrated digital network usnng the Internet.
Other measures include lifting strict regulations covering building materials, strengthening the watchdog Fair Trade Commission and extend copyright to 50 years.

As part of its action plan, Japan said it has already cut tariffs on 697 goods such as textiles, chemicals, steel and non- ferrous metals in April 1996, two years ahead of the date promised under the Uruguay Rounds.
